name: Tarshish
title: Son of Javan and ancestor of a coastal people
summary: Tarshish was a son of Javan and grandson of Japheth, who in turn was a son of Noah. He is regarded as the ancestor of a people living by the coast, likely connected to distant Tarshish (Tartessos) in the western Mediterranean region. The name Tarshish is also associated with seafaring and long-distance trade in the Bible.

keyEvents.title: Mentioned in Noah's genealogy
keyEvents.description: Tarshish is mentioned as a son of Javan in the post-flood genealogy, as part of the table of nations in Genesis.

keyEvents.title: The Table of Nations in 1 Chronicles
keyEvents.description: Tarshish is mentioned again in the genealogy in 1 Chronicles as one of Javan's sons, confirming his place among the origins of the peoples.

keyEvents.title: Tarsis Ships and Wealth
keyEvents.description: The name Tarsis is linked to distant sea voyages and trade. King Solomon and King Jehoshaphat had Tarsis ships that brought gold, silver, ivory, and exotic goods.

keyEvents.title: The Prophecy about Tarsis in Isaiah
keyEvents.description: The prophet Isaiah delivers a prophecy concerning Tarsis, describing the destruction of its ships and trading activities as a sign of God's judgment against pride and wealth.

keyEvents.title: Jonah's Escape Route to Tarsis
keyEvents.description: When the prophet Jonah tried to flee from God's call, he boarded a ship bound for Tarsis, which represented the farthest place one could travel—away from God's presence.

keyEvents.title: Tarsis in Ezekiel's Prophecies
keyEvents.description: In Ezekiel's lament over Tyre, Tarsis is mentioned as an important trading partner that exchanged silver, iron, tin, and lead with the powerful commercial city.
